surfaces.part: tiled roof plane (full cell, repeating tile courses)

answer.evidence: The whole cell (rows 0-15, constant width 15) is one sloped roof plane of teal tile courses. Each course is a light edge line (L=168 at rows 1, 5, 9, 13) over mid-tone tile rows and dark shadow rows, so the roof-plane evidence (c) is present. The bottom edge line at row 13 is followed by the shadow rows 14-15. No vertical wall, lintel face or door face is drawn below the roof, so there is no front face of 3 or more rows. The cell is a roof fragment, not a complete building with a top and a front, so it reads as a flat slab by the definitions.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny teal icon, roughly 14x28 px at 2x, with a few horizontal stripes. It is not a whole building: it has no roof, walls, door or windows. It shows 5 visible tones against 12 and 10 for the references, and 0% near-flat coverage only because the object is so small. The measured 0% neutral edge share is not meaningful because there is no real outline. Shading is shallow, with 2-3 teal steps against about 6 per material on the references. It has no tile scallops, plaster speckle or stone-by-stone shading. It would look far thinner and flatter than either reference, and it does not match the kind.

answer.evidence: The whole 15px-wide, 16-row tile is one repeating pattern of roof tile courses. The same course pattern runs to the bottom edge, so row 15 is just another course shadow. There is no wall, lintel or eave-and-face transition and no vertical south face of 3 or more rows. This is a sloped roof surface fill with no front face, so it reads as a flat slab.
